pr_title: Update TextureRect when its Texture is modified directly
pr_body:
This change makes `TextureRect` properly react to `ImageTexture::_change_notify()`

Fixes #32349
pr_comments: That function is only used for the editor. Connect to "changed" signal instead.

Thanks @reduz. I've updated my changes to make things work outside of the editor:
- Now `TextureRect` uses `changed` signal from its internal `Texture` to update
- I've made similar changes in `Sprite` to make texture updates work outside of the editor as well
- `Object::change_receptors` and add/remove functions are now inlined and editor only, since they are not functional otherwise
CC @neikeq to check that the `Object` changes wouldn't imply the core API hash consistency between tools/non-tools.
If needed I can make a separate PR for the changes in `Object`. It's not needed for this fix, just a little optimization.
Thanks for the feedback, I've just reverted the changes in `Object`.

issue_context.title: TextureRect size doesn't update when its texture changes size
issue_context.body:
Windows 10 64 bits
Godot 3.1.1

Similar to closed #20614 , if I change the size of a texture previously assigned to a `TextureRect`, the node does not update its size. 
This doesn't happen with sprites.

Project:
[TextureRectNotResizingIfTextureRecreated.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/3649573/TextureRectNotResizingIfTextureRecreated.zip)
comments:
Yeah, if using
```
	yield(VisualServer, "frame_post_draw")
	print(_texture_rect_with_forced_swap.rect_size)
```

the real `rect_size` will be displayed.

This issue is actually much deeper and isn't just isolated to `TextureRect`, it happens in a lot of nodes inherited from `Control`. From my experience with extreme UI development, my solutions over the years to obtain the correct  `rect_size`, is to   use a mixture of

 ```
modulate.a = 0
yield(get_tree(), "idle_frame") or yield(VisualServer, "frame_post_draw")
modulate.a = 1
```
I created a PR about this last year or so (might have been on my old deleted account, and can't find it).
 
The PR is probably the solution, but it  might need to happen in `Control` as well.

Basically, it's a good rule of thumb to always try yielding VisualServer's `frame_post_draw` signal if your `rect_sizes` are **not displaying what you think they should**. 95% of the time, yielding that signal   will fix any UI sizing issue you might run into.

 This is **very important** to future developers because I've spent a lot of time trying to figure out why a node wasn't resizing correctly, and then it ultimately was fixed by just slapping a `idle_frame` or `frame_post_draw` signal in code.

Yeah having to wait for the engine to draw can be very limiting. See how complexity can stem from that when one has to workaround it: https://godotengine.org/qa/51562/get_visible_line_count-returning-previous-change-labels. 1-frame delay can stem really hard-to-track bugs if other logic depends on it (not to mention possible interruptions).

But in this situation it looks like it could still be fixed, because the engine knows the size of the texture right away, and it does update if I explicitely re-assign the `texture` property. I understand the UI needs to defer things sometimes due to complicated layout relationships, but here this is not the case. There should not be a need to wait for a frame here (it doesnt works if I do anyways xD).

tbh I could use a sprite to workaround this, my current use case is quite simple.
Lol, I can totally relate to that QA post. I swear, I could write a book about `rect_size` and `idle_frame` 😆

review_comments: This is good, because change receptor is only meant to be used by the editor. It needs to remain but the function will change for 4.0. If you see this used in normal scene nodes, its good to change it like here.
